candidates.name: Myocarditis
support_spans: ST-segment elevation on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
diffuse contraction band necrosis with several lymphocytes in cardiac muscle
candidates.why: The patient presented with cardiac symptoms and had elevated cardiac markers, which suggests myocarditis.

candidates.name: Pericarditis
support_spans: Pericardial effusion: 70 mL clear fluid
candidates.why: The patient had a significant amount of pericardial effusion, which is a characteristic of pericarditis.

candidates.name: COVID-19 myocarditis
support_spans: SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
Elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6)
candidates.why: The patient was positive for SARS-CoV-2 and had elevated inflammatory cytokines, which suggests a COVID-19-related myocarditis.

candidates.name: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
support_spans: Thrombopenia
CD42b immunohistochemical staining showed platelet aggregation in cardiac microvessels
candidates.why: The patient had thrombocytopenia and platelet aggregation in cardiac microvessels, which are characteristic of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.

candidates.name: COVID-19 myocarditis
support_spans: SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
candidates.why: A positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen test is decisive for diagnosing COVID-19 myocarditis.

candidates.name: Myocardial infarction
support_spans: Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
contradict_spans: No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed
candidates.why: Elevated cardiac markers are decisive for diagnosing myocardial infarction, but the absence of coronary artery disease makes this diagnosis less likely.
